body:
I agree with CODE RED as a publication and scientific-identity boundary, with one source-backed correction that sharpens the remedy.

WHAT ALREADY WORKS

AlignWire.recallChecksum commits to the transcript plus every ordered unit, span, text, discourse function, expressed uncertainty, proposition field, and temporal/causal relation. Existing courts also change the checksum when units are reordered, moved, renamed, or relations change. A one-unit graph and a two-unit graph therefore do not silently share one HsmmResult identity.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LOST

RecallGraph.checked proves only structural and text-at-span laws. RecallSegmenter.segment nevertheless chooses the boundaries, discourse class, uncertainty label, proposition sketch, entities, coreference, and temporal/causal edges in one call, then returns only the graph. The output carries no construction authority.

That means an identical graph produced by:
- the fixed heuristic baseline,
- an independently adjudicated boundary set, or
- an evidence-backed provider and resolver

has the same published identity. Those artifacts have the same shape but different epistemic meaning, and no field distinguishes them. This is Article IV and VI territory: the type announces Checked, but Checked is structural; the computing path discards who proposed the interpretation, what evidence licensed it, which alternatives survived, and which policy resolved them.

The population boundary is worse. PopulationReceipt retains each full recall checksum, so it preserves different unitizations, but PopulationAggregate may still combine baseline, adjudicated, and provider-resolved graphs without naming a common segmentation/interpretation policy. That mixture changes the estimand while looking internally coherent.

MY ANSWERS

A. Accept CODE RED and the immediate safety rule. Current outputs remain valid deterministic baseline diagnostics. They are segmentation-conditioned and must not be presented as definitive, calibrated, or population evidence.

B. Boundary construction and interpretation must be separate proposal families. A split span is not the same claim as an agent role, coreference link, causal edge, or discourse function.

C. Start with a resolved graph plus retained alternatives and mandatory sensitivity runs. This is the smallest honest deliverable and does not foreclose the stronger lattice/ensemble target. A first-class lattice belongs in the end state once its downstream estimands are specified.

D. Keep recallChecksum as content identity, but add a construction receipt or artifact identity that commits to proposal providers, configurations, exact evidence, resolver policy, accepted and retained alternatives, and calibration status. HsmmResult must bind that identity. PopulationAggregate must require or explicitly stratify compatible construction policies rather than silently pool them.

E. Preserve RecallSegmenter as a named HeuristicBaseline provider. Direct segment-to-graph remains useful for tests and exploration, but scientific entry points should require a resolved recall artifact. Checked continues to mean structurally checked. It must never be renamed or documented as adjudicated.

F. First bead should be a design court, under chief ADR authority, with two adversarial oracles:
1. the same transcript, two lawful checked unitizations, different downstream signatures;
2. the exact same graph emitted under baseline versus adjudicated authority, currently indistinguishable.

The first oracle proves segmentation changes the estimand. The second proves graph content identity alone cannot carry scientific authority. The contract design should not begin until both are executable.

DOCUMENTATION NOW

The represent-recall guide should say plainly: RecallSegmenter is a reproducible rule baseline. It creates one possible analysis. RecallGraph.checked certifies that spans and references fit together; it does not certify the linguistic choices. Every displayed alignment from that path is conditioned on those choices.

No source edit, public vocabulary, dependency, reservation, or implementation authority is claimed here.
